newsitem.title: USA: Grigsby "unresigns" from U.S. investment bank.
newsitem.headline: Grigsby "unresigns" from U.S. investment bank.

text.p: Calvin Grigsby, who resigned last month from Grigsby Brandford & Co. under the cloud of a federal probe, has rejoined his investment banking firm, officials said Monday.

"Calvin has told us that he is going to come back into the firm," Dade County, Florida, Finance Director Ed Marquez said during a meeting of the Dade County Finance and Trust Funds Committee. "He has unresigned."
Others involved with the firm confirmed Grigsby's return but declined to discuss his reasons.
Officials in Grigsby's office in San Francisco said the firm was now called Grigsby & Associates. They would not discuss the reasons for the name change or Grigsby's status.

The management shake-up at Grigsby Brandford, the nation's largest minority-owned investment banking firm, began Sept. 17, when Grigsby, the firm's founder and long-time chairman, abruptly announced his resignation.
After he left, it was disclosed that authorities were investigating bond deals the firm handled in Dade County. Grigsby has not been charged with any wrongdoing in the probe.
In a recent statement, Grigsby's attorney said his client "strongly maintains his innocence."
Marquez said Grigsby told him earlier Monday that he resigned last month because he felt it was best for the firm and that the firm could continue under the guidance of other top executives.

But earlier this month, newly appointed Chairman Napoleon Brandford and President Suzanne Shank said they were leaving. Both Brandford and Shank announced plans to join Muriel Siebert & Co. to open a new municipal bond unit for the company. About 40 employees of Grigsby Brandford are expected to join Muriel Siebert.

Despite the management turmoil, Marquez said Grigsby's firm remained senior manager on a proposed $168 million arena bond for Dade County, which includes Miami, if voters approved the issue in a Nov. 5 ballot.
